meta.title: PageTide: Open-Source Research Assistant for Papers
meta.description: PageTide is an open-source research assistant that learns your research profile and recommends new papers daily. No account, no telemetry. macOS and Windows.

editorial.title: More papers is not the problem. Finding yours is.
body: About 20,000 new papers appear every day1. A handful of them matter to your work, and no one can read a feed that long. Most tools answer with a bigger feed. PageTide answers with a smaller one.

It learns a research profile from what you mark useful or not relevant, then ranks each day’s new papers on your own computer. The profile is a list of plain words you can read, correct and delete. AI is optional, and its job is to explain a paper to you, not to choose it for you. Unlike a chat-based AI research assistant, PageTide does not ask you to describe what you want each time. It reads your feedback, keeps a research profile you can edit, and turns it into paper recommendations that improve the more you use it.
Your library, your PDFs, your notes and your profile stay on your computer. There is no account, no server and no telemetry.
editorial.footnote: 1 OpenAlex lists 626,339 journal articles published in September 2026, about 20,900 a day; queried 2026-10-25. Source: OpenAlex.

get.first_title: First launch: the app is not signed
get.first_lead: PageTide is an independent open-source project with no paid code-signing certificate, so your system will warn you the first time. This is expected.
get.first_mac: Unzip, drag PageTide to Applications, then right-click it and choose Open. Or go to System Settings → Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.
get.first_mac_damaged: If macOS says the app is damaged, run this in Terminal:
get.first_win: When SmartScreen says “Windows protected your PC”, click More info, then Run anyway. The installer is per-user and needs no administrator rights.
get.req_mac: macOS on Apple Silicon (M1 or later) or Intel.
get.keys_lead: The core (picking, the profile, the library) works offline with no key. Optional services use your own key, stored on your computer.

contribute.title: Contributions welcome
contribute.body: PageTide is a research assistant built in the open. Bug reports, feature ideas, documentation and translation fixes, and pull requests are all welcome, and small fixes count as much as new features. For a bigger change, please open an issue first so we can agree on the direction.

features.title: A research assistant for every step of your reading

items.alt: The Today screen: a ranked list of new papers, each with a one-line AI preview and Save, Not interested and Too hard buttons.
items.title: Daily picks, explained
items.body: Each morning a short list of new papers, ranked against your profile, each with a one-line reason. One optional AI call previews up to 20 picks at once.

items.alt: The profile screen: the keywords behind every pick, with weights, pins and an undo list.
items.title: A profile that keeps itself current
items.body: Every paper you save or mark Not interested refines your profile, so it sharpens the more you use it. It stays a short list of plain keywords, yours to adjust at any time.

items.alt: The library graph: saved papers grouped into directions and linked to related work.
items.title: A library that connects itself
items.body: Saved papers become a list and a graph of related work. Open-access PDFs are archived on your computer, and nothing is reorganized until you confirm.

items.alt: The PDF reader with a highlighted sentence and an answer to a follow-up question beside the page.
items.title: Highlight, ask, understand
items.body: Read the PDF inside PageTide, select a sentence, then translate it or ask about it. The answer appears beside the page.

items.alt: The import screen with PDF files, folders, BibTeX, RIS and CSL JSON.
items.title: Bring what you have
items.body: Import PDF files or folders (subfolders become categories), or a Zotero collection exported as BibTeX, RIS or CSL JSON.

items.alt: The weekly report: what you saved, what you skipped and which directions grew.
items.title: A weekly report
items.body: What you saved, what you skipped and which directions grew this week, so the shape of your reading is visible.
